extracted.intended_audience: inventors, applicants, IP practitioners, and national IP offices dealing with ARIPO-region IP filings
extracted.subtask_description: A regional practice guide describing registration routes, substantive eligibility standards, application contents, fees, timelines, renewals, and exclusions for patents, utility models, trade marks, industrial designs, traditional knowledge, and copyright under ARIPO/Harare Protocol frameworks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice of registration route (national vs regional vs international)
rubrics_metrics.description: IP protection in ARIPO can be secured nationally through Member State offices or regionally through ARIPO; ARIPO is not party to international IP registration routes so international filings are addressed at Member State level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A national route is suitable when protection is required in the Member State only. A regional ARIPO route is suitable when multi-state protection is required. Consider whether substantive examination is required, number of jurisdictions needed, cost-effectiveness, and time-effectiveness when choosing between ARIPO and national routes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional representation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Foreign applicants whose principal place of business is outside ARIPO Member States must appoint a local agent; representation is mandatory in some filing types for non-residents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ARIPO accepts signed powers of attorney without legalisation or notarisation; scanned copies emailed are sufficient, though some agents may request originals. A list of ARIPO representatives is available on ARIPO's website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent application contents (required documents)
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent application must contain: a request on the prescribed form; a description; one or more claims; drawings, if any; an abstract; the applicant’s details (name, nationality, legal status, physical address); designation of one or more Member States; Deed of Assignment if applicant is not the inventor; certified copy of the priority document if priority claimed; prescribed application fees; sequence listing if nucleotide/amino acid sequences disclosed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure inclusion of sequence listings where applicable. Indicate designated states clearly when filing through national offices to show the application is regional via ARIPO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentability substantive criteria (novelty, inventive step, industrial applicability)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any invention in all fields of technology can be registered provided that it is new (absolute novelty), involves an inventive step (not obvious to a person skilled in the art), and is susceptible to industrial application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Novelty must be absolute and not anticipated by prior art. Inventive step assessed with regard to prior art. Industrial applicability includes use in any kind of industry (including agriculture). Also must be patentable under applicable national law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent subject-matter exclusions under Harare Protocol
rubrics_metrics.description: ARIPO will not consider as inventions: discoveries, scientific theories, mathematical methods; aesthetic creations; schemes, rules and methods for mental acts, games, business, and computer programs; presentations of information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additionally, ARIPO patents will not be granted where commercial exploitation would be contrary to 'ordre public' or morality; plant or animal varieties or essentially biological processes for production of plants or animals (except microbiological processes/products); methods for treatment of the human or animal body by surgery or therapy and diagnostic methods practised on the body (products for use in these methods may be patentable).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent filing locations and methods
rubrics_metrics.description: ARIPO patent applications can be filed at ARIPO headquarters in Zimbabwe or at IP Offices of ARIPO Member States. Applications filed through ARIPO can be filed electronically, by email, registered mail, fax, courier, or in person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Online ARIPO application fees have a 20% discount to encourage online filing. Applications filed at national offices should clearly indicate they are regional applications through ARIPO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent fees, designation fees, and annuity payments
rubrics_metrics.description: Fees include an application fee (paper/online rates), state designation fees (per designated state), mandatory annuity fee for PCT-based applications, and annual maintenance (renewal) fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fees are payable through ARIPO in USD. Fee schedules are published on ARIPO's website and reviewed regularly; confirm latest amounts online. Professional fees vary—obtain quotes from at least three ARIPO-accredited professionals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent prosecution timelines and grant duration
rubrics_metrics.description: ARIPO patent applications are substantively examined and take 24-36 months on average to complete registration (if no objections). Protection lasts 20 years from the filing date, subject to annual maintenance fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Renewal fees payable up to the 19th year; late renewal fees include a surcharge and a monthly penalty per month or fraction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence listing requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: If the patent application contains disclosure of one or more nucleotide and/or amino acid sequences, a sequence listing must be provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the sequence listing in the prescribed format to avoid formality issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Utility model definition and eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: A utility model under the Harare Protocol includes forms/configurations/dispositions of elements of everyday use, tools, electrical/electronic circuitry, instruments, handicraft, mechanisms or other objects, including micro-organisms or other self-replicable material, products of genetic resources, herbal and nutritional formulations that give new effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A utility model will be protected provided it is new and industrially applicable and is a registrable invention under applicable national law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Utility model exclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Under ARIPO, utility models will not be granted for inventions whose exploitation is contrary to 'ordre public' or morality; plant or animal varieties or essentially biological processes for production of plants or animals (not applying to microbiological processes/products); inventions related to treatment of humans or animals or pharmaceutical inventions (to avoid undue restrictions to access to medical care).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also general exclusions mirror patent exclusions: discoveries, mathematical methods, aesthetic creations, business methods, computer programs, presentations of information are not considered inventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Utility model application contents
rubrics_metrics.description: A utility model application must contain: a request on the prescribed form; a description; one or more claims; drawings, if any; an abstract; designation of one or more Member States; Deed of Assignment if applicant not inventor; certified priority copy if claimed; prescribed application fees; applicant’s details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications filed via Member State offices should indicate they are ARIPO regional applications. Online filing discounts may apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Utility model prosecution timelines and duration
rubrics_metrics.description: ARIPO utility model applications are substantively examined and typically take 24-36 months to register (assuming minimal official actions and no objections). ARIPO-registered utility models are protected for 10 years from filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Renewal fees are payable up to the 10th year. Ensure utility model protection exists in designated states before designating them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trade mark application contents (required documents)
rubrics_metrics.description: A trade mark application must contain: full name, nationality and address of applicant; a completed application form (form M1); a designation of one or more Member States; a list of goods/services per the Nice Classification; representation of the mark; certified copy of priority document if priority claimed; signed power of attorney if represented (no notarisation required); a declaration of actual use or intention to use; prescribed fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure goods/services lists follow the current Nice Classification edition at filing. Foreign applicants must appoint a local agent.

rubrics_metrics.name: What qualifies as a trade mark
rubrics_metrics.description: A trade mark is any sign, name, word, device, brand, heading, signature, letters or numbers, or combination thereof that helps consumers distinguish goods/services and identify brands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include logos, slogans, T-shirt brands, family symbols, event names. Use declarations of use or intent to use appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trade mark absolute and relative grounds for refusal (what cannot be registered)
rubrics_metrics.description: Marks cannot be registered if: incapable of distinguishing; contain false indications or are deceptive; contrary to law/public order/morality; likely to cause confusion with earlier marks; constitute a name/likeness without authorization; contain head of state depiction; resemble armorial bearing/flag/emblem; contain title/abbreviation of international intergovernmental organisation; comprise Olympic symbol; designate kind/quality/quantity/purpose/characteristics of goods/services; are customary in language or trade; consist exclusively of certain shapes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific shape exclusions include shapes resulting from nature of goods, shapes necessary to obtain technical result, or shapes giving substantial inherent value. Assessment of confusion and distinctiveness occurs under Member State law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trade mark filing locations, methods, and fees
rubrics_metrics.description: ARIPO trade mark applications can be filed in person, electronically, by mail or fax at ARIPO headquarters or at Member State IP Offices. Official ARIPO fees (paper/online rates) apply and are payable in USD.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ARIPO uses a multiclass and state designation system resembling the Madrid system; Member States should amend laws to recognize ARIPO and Madrid marks. Fee schedules and application forms are available on ARIPO's website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trade mark prosecution timeline and duration
rubrics_metrics.description: Trade mark registration typically takes 15-18 months from filing to completion (assuming no delays or oppositions) and includes an opposition period of 3 months. Protection lasts 10 years from filing and is renewable for 10-year periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Renewal and designation fees are per class/country as published in fee schedules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial design application contents and formalities
rubrics_metrics.description: An industrial design application must contain: fully completed request form (Form 28); a reproduction of the industrial designs to be registered; a designation of contracting states in which protection is sought; payment of fees or undertaking to pay within 21 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants may file at ARIPO HQ or national IP offices; representation is mandatory for applicants not resident or not having principal place of business in a contracting state.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial design substantive eligibility (what qualifies)
rubrics_metrics.description: An industrial design is the ornamental aesthetic aspect of a useful article that makes it attractive and adds commercial value; design protection grants exclusive rights against unauthorized copying or imitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design protection aims to increase marketability; assess novelty and aesthetic distinctiveness relative to prior designs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial design exclusions under Harare Protocol
rubrics_metrics.description: ARIPO industrial designs will not be granted for inventions whose commercial exploitation would be contrary to 'ordre public' or morality; plant or animal varieties or essentially biological processes for production of plants or animals (not applying to microbiological processes/products); methods for treatment of the human or animal body by surgery, therapy or diagnostic methods (subject to exceptions for products).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: What cannot be registered is also determined by Member State national laws; applicants should ensure design protection exists in designated states before designating them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial design prosecution timeline and duration
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications usually take 8-12 months to complete registration, including a 6-month period for States to examine whether the design will have legal effect in their territories. ARIPO-route design registrations are valid for 15 years (no possibility of extension except where Member State law provides otherwise).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Renewal fees are payable within 6 months before expiry; late payment possible within 6-month grace period. Fees payable per designated state.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination regimes and Member State discretion
rubrics_metrics.description: ARIPO carries out formal examination of designs; Member States may carry out substantive examination if required by national laws. For patents and utility models, ARIPO conducts substantive examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This affects processing time: Member State offices often conduct only formality checks and may be faster for single-country protection; ARIPO substantive examination can be preferable when examination is required or multi-jurisdiction protection is sought.

rubrics_metrics.name: Utility model and patent strategic considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Decisions between ARIPO and national routes for patents/utility models are guided by cost, number of jurisdictions, substantive examination requirements, and duration of protection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ARIPO is usually more cost-effective for multi-state protection. For utility models, national routes may be preferable if protection needed in a single state or if national duration differs significantly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Traditional knowledge and expressions of folklore eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Traditional knowledge: knowledge originating from a local/traditional community resulting from intellectual activity in a traditional context (including know-how, skills, innovations) that is generated, preserved and transmitted in a traditional and intergenerational context, distinctively associated with a community, and integral to cultural identity with custodianship/guardianship. Expressions of folklore: verbal, musical, movement, or tangible expressions that are products of creative and cumulative intellectual activity characteristic of a community's cultural identity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protection extends to knowledge/folklore that meet these criteria; special categories with spiritual or sacred value may require notification to appropriate authorities for evidence purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Traditional knowledge and folklore application requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications must be made on ARIPO Form T1 (traditional knowledge) or Form F1 (expressions of folklore) and must include: name and address of applicant; Member State nationality of applicant; request for registration; purpose of registration; economic/social/scientific/technical/environmental or other benefits likely to accrue to owners/community; proposed mechanism for equitable sharing of benefits; designation of Contracting State or communities possessing/sharing the subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protection will not be subject to formalities; national competent authorities and ARIPO may maintain registers or records for transparency and preservation, subject to policies and needs of holders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Traditional knowledge and folklore processing time, fees, and duration
rubrics_metrics.description: Registration typically takes 6-12 months. ARIPO application and registration/publication fees apply (example: application fee 50 USD, registration/publication 50 USD for both TK and folklore in published tables). Traditional knowledge protection lasts as long as the protection criteria are fulfilled; for an individual, protection is 25 years following exploitation beyond traditional context (not renewable). Expressions of folklore protected as long as criteria are fulfilled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm current fees on ARIPO website. Applicants should include mechanisms for equitable sharing in applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright voluntary registration under Kampala Protocol
rubrics_metrics.description: Kampala Protocol establishes a regional system for voluntary registration and notification of copyright and related rights to provide presumption of authorship/ownership and to coordinate registration across Member States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registration is voluntary; copyright exists automatically on creation per Berne Convention principles. The implementing regulations of the Protocol are yet to be established; authors/owners may apply to national authorities or ARIPO to register particulars in the database.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforcement responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: ARIPO does not directly enforce IP rights among its Member States; enforcement relies on each Member State to enforce IP rights under local laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Right holders should enforce their IP rights according to the local regulations and procedures of each Member State.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation scope for ARIPO filings (which states may be designated)
rubrics_metrics.description: Not all ARIPO Member States are available for designation for all IP types; typically 20 Member States can be designated for patents, utility models and industrial designs (Mauritius and Somalia excluded); for trade marks, 13 countries can be designated (list provided).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check the current list of designable Member States before filing; enforcement and availability of specific IP rights may vary by Member State law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional fees recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: Professional (agent/attorney) fees vary by level of experience and time spent; applicants are advised to obtain comparative quotes from at least three ARIPO-accredited professionals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A list of ARIPO-accredited IP agents is available on ARIPO's website; plan for both official government fees and professional fees when budgeting.
